entries.appliesTo: Alabama public K-12 schools (elementary, middle, and high) and public school students

sources.curriculum: § 16-46B-2(a)(1) — 'each public high school shall offer at least one authentic computer science course from a department-approved list'; § 16-46B-2(d) — 'shall include, but not be limited to, instruction in the concepts of computer science as defined in Section 16-46B-1'
sources.graduationReq: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'Beginning with the graduating class of 2032, all public school students shall demonstrate digital literacy by earning at least one credit in a department-approved, high school or college-level computer science course, or by completing a department-approved course with embedded computer science skills and experiences.'
sources.enforcer: § 16-46B-2(e) — 'The enforcement of this section shall comply with Section 16-1-11.1.'

flags: AI-adjacent only: artificial intelligence appears solely in the amended definition of computer science (§ 16-46B-1(2) — 'their emerging technologies, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence'); the bill imposes no AI-specific duty beyond curriculum content.

State Department of Education (not schools) bears standards-setting duties: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'The department shall develop and publish a set of minimum standards' and 'shall publish a list of high school or college-level computer science courses'.
Graduation requirement expressly does not add credits: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'This requirement shall not result in an increase in the number of credits required for graduation.'
No penalty provision in this text; enforcement routed by cross-reference to Section 16-1-11.1 (rule 4 — no penaltyMax coded).
Effective October 1, 2026 (Section 2); graduation requirement begins with the class of 2032.
